intervals.label: underground experiments
intervals.note: 'since 1960' is the paper's wording for the series of underground experiments; the end is the year the proton-decay experiment stopped data taking: 'Since the management of KGF mines decided to start closing the mines in 1993, the proton decay experiment stopped data taking in 1993.' A 1951 cosmic-ray measurement in the Champion Reef mine preceded the laboratory (CERN Courier).
intervals.quote: A series of experiments underground has been carried out deep underground in KGF since 1960.

intervals.label: mines closed; laboratory ended
intervals.note: Terminal event: the laboratory ended with the closure of the mines, which the paper says started in 1993. Another account says the laboratory ceased operating in 1992; that account is a magazine article not used here.
intervals.quote: Since the management of KGF mines decided to start closing the mines in 1993, the proton decay experiment stopped data taking in 1993.

name: Kolar Gold Fields underground laboratory
notes: Operator not stated in any fetched source (the experiments were run by the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research with Osaka City University); left null.

summary.plain: An underground laboratory in the deep Kolar Gold Fields mines of southern India. From 1960 until the mines closed in 1993 it hosted experiments that saw the first atmospheric neutrinos and searched for proton decay.
summary.technical: Underground laboratory in the Kolar Gold Fields mines (Karnataka, India), at levels down to about 2.3 km of rock: cosmic-ray muon depth-intensity measurements, the 1965 atmospheric-neutrino telescopes, and the Phase I/II proton-decay detectors; ended with the mine closures from 1993.
